content.user_title: Manage MongoDB Atlas Organizations with Azure .NET
content.value_statement: Azure Marketplace integration for MongoDB Atlas requires specific ARM models and workflows. This skill provides focused .NET guidance for provisioning and managing organization resources.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the required Azure Resource Manager, MongoDB Atlas, and identity packages.
Explains authentication with DefaultAzureCredential and ArmClient.
Provides C# workflows to create, retrieve, list, update, and delete MongoDB Atlas organization resources.
Documents marketplace, offer, user, partner, provisioning, and subscription status models.
Demonstrates resource group and subscription-level organization discovery.
Explains asynchronous operations, status polling, resource identifiers, and common Azure errors.
limitations: Covers MongoDB Atlas organizations exposed through Azure Resource Manager only.
Does not manage Atlas clusters, databases, collections, users, or roles.
Requires valid Azure credentials, permissions, subscription details, and marketplace offer information.
Examples use placeholders and require validation against the target environment and current SDK version.

use_cases.title: Provision an Atlas organization
use_cases.description: Create an Azure-managed Atlas organization with marketplace, administrator, partner, and tagging details.

use_cases.title: Standardize marketplace onboarding
use_cases.description: Build repeatable organization provisioning and lifecycle workflows for Azure platform services.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot ARM workflows
use_cases.description: Inspect provisioning states, subscription status, resource identifiers, permissions, and common request failures.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the SDK scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what Azure.ResourceManager.MongoDBAtlas manages. Compare its organization scope with Atlas cluster and database management.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is selecting the correct management API.

prompt_templates.title: Plan organization creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a C# workflow to create an Atlas organization in {resource_group}. List required marketplace, user, partner, authentication, and validation inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is preparing an Azure Marketplace integration.

prompt_templates.title: Design inventory and tagging
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an asynchronous C# workflow to list Atlas organizations across {subscription}. Update approved tags and report provisioning states without changing other properties.
prompt_templates.scenario: A platform engineer needs consistent inventory metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Atlas organization lifecycle design: {design}. Identify permission, idempotency, polling, failure recovery, deletion, billing, and environment validation concerns.
prompt_templates.scenario: An architect is validating production automation.

output_examples.input: Explain whether this SDK can create an Atlas cluster.
output_examples.output: This SDK manages Atlas organizations represented as Azure resources. Use the MongoDB Atlas API or another supported tool for clusters.

output_examples.input: List the inputs needed to create an organization.
output: Azure subscription, resource group, location, and authenticated ARM client.
Marketplace publisher, offer, plan, term, and billing subscription details.
Organization name and administrator email or user principal name.
Optional tags and user profile fields.

output_examples.input: Suggest checks for a long-running create operation.
output: Choose whether to wait for completion or poll after starting.
Track completion and provisioning state before dependent work.
Capture Azure request failures and marketplace subscription errors.
Verify the final resource identifier and organization data.

best_practices: Use asynchronous SDK methods and handle long-running operations explicitly.
Validate permissions, offer identifiers, billing details, and administrator data before provisioning.
Use resource identifiers and provisioning states to confirm the intended resource before updates or deletion.
anti_patterns: Do not use this SDK for Atlas clusters, databases, collections, users, or roles.
Do not place real subscription identifiers or personal data in reusable prompts and examples.
Do not delete or replace organization properties without explicit approval and current-state verification.

faq.question: What resources does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers MongoDB Atlas organizations represented as Azure Resource Manager resources.

faq.question: Can it manage Atlas clusters?
faq.answer: No. Manage clusters through the MongoDB Atlas API or another supported management tool.

faq.question: Which authentication method is demonstrated?
faq.answer: The examples use DefaultAzureCredential with ArmClient.

faq.question: Which inputs are required for creation?
faq.answer: You need Azure resource details, marketplace offer data, billing subscription information, organization details, and an administrator identity.

faq.question: How are long-running operations handled?
faq.answer: The SDK can wait for completion or start an operation and poll its status later.

faq.question: Should the examples run unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders and verify permissions, SDK compatibility, marketplace terms, and environment-specific requirements.
